name: Grand Hyatt Kauai Resort & Spa
insider_take: This oceanfront paradise sits on 50 acres of pristine Poipu Beach coastline, where endangered Hawaiian monk seals regularly sunbathe on the golden sand right outside your window.
whats_special: The resort features a spectacular 150,000-gallon saltwater swimming lagoon with tropical fish, plus Hawaii's largest spa at 25,000 square feet. The property's Tidepools restaurant offers romantic overwater dining pavilions connected by torchlit walkways, while the championship Poipu Bay Golf Course designed by Robert Trent Jones Jr. hosts PGA Grand Slam events.
pro_tip: Book treatments at ANARA Spa during sunset hours – the oceanfront treatment rooms offer unobstructed views of Kauai's legendary green flash phenomenon as the sun dips below the horizon.
dont_miss: The daily 4 PM torch lighting ceremony at Shipwreck Beach, followed by drinks at Stevenson's Library bar where vintage maritime artifacts tell tales of Kauai's shipwreck history. The nearby Spouting Horn blowhole creates 50-foot water geysers at high tide, and Waimea Canyon – the "Grand Canyon of the Pacific" – is just a 45-minute scenic drive away.
pros: Stunning oceanfront location on Poipu Beach
World-class ANARA Spa with traditional Hawaiian treatments
Multiple pools including lagoon-style pool with waterfalls
Exceptional dining options with farm-to-table cuisine
Hyatt Prive benefits including room upgrades and resort credits
cons: Large resort property may feel less intimate
